nodes.label: Conscious clothing purchases

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_000
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What has been the primary focus of the fast fashion market in response to consumer demands?
nodes.answer: The primary focus of the fast fashion market has been to provide large quantities of low-cost clothing in very short periods in response to consumer demands.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the ease of fast fashion impact the expansion of rental clothing services?
nodes.answer: The ease of fast fashion creates implications for the expansion of rental clothing services, making it a challenge to attract consumers away from the convenience of fast fashion.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What were the key findings of the conjoint experiment regarding the importance of different attributes in fashion purchasing decisions?
nodes.answer: In the conjoint experiment, participants rated product ratings as the most important attribute in fashion purchasing decisions, followed closely by price. Sustainability labelling of clothing items was found to be less important than product ratings and price.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How will counting externalities in apparel manufacturing impact prices?
nodes.answer: When externalities are considered, apparel prices will rise to reflect the value society places on global sustainability and prosperity for future generations.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_004
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What type of specialization does the platform offering ethical clothing have?
nodes.answer: The platform offering ethical clothing specializes in per item rental.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_005
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What exception was observed in the comparison of T-shirt life cycle GHG emissions between owned and rental garments?
nodes.answer: The T-shirt results between owned and rental are comparable even though it is dry-cleaned in rental because the T-shirt was set to be worn and laundered frequently when owned, making the impact from domestic laundry comparable to the dry-cleaning impact when rented.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_006
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: In terms of GHG emissions per wear, why was renting garments found to have a smaller impact compared to owning them?
nodes.answer: The reason renting garments showed a smaller GHG impact per wear compared to owning them is because the lifetime wear count was assumed to be greater when rented, leading to reduced emissions overall.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_007
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What is the fibre content of the T-shirt in the life cycle inventory (LCD)?
nodes.answer: The T-shirt in the life cycle inventory has a fibre content of 100% linen.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_008
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Why do entrepreneurs believe that renting clothes will replace fast fashion?
nodes.answer: Entrepreneurs believe that renting clothes will replace fast fashion because it offers a more sustainable and economically viable alternative to traditional retail. By renting clothes, consumers can access a wider variety of items without the commitment of ownership, while also reducing their environmental footprint.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_009
nodes.label: Ethics and Regulation
nodes.question: Is the clothing produced in an environmentally respectful manner?
nodes.answer: Yes, it is very important for the clothing to be produced in an environmentally respectful manner.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_010
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Is the brand of the clothing well-known?
nodes.answer: Yes, it is important for the clothing to be from a well-known brand.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_011
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do consumers generally feel about eco-fashion products based on the literature?
nodes.answer: Consumers have a conflicted relation towards eco-fashion products, as highlighted in the literature.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_012
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does meaning relate to practices, and why is it significant?
nodes.answer: Meaning is tied to practices as it involves mental and emotional aspects that can influence one's engagement with certain activities. Understanding the social and symbolic meanings attached to practices can impact individual decisions and behaviours, making it a significant aspect to consider in sustainable fashion consumption.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_013
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why did respondents report a drop in their apparel spending during COVID-19?
nodes.answer: Respondents reported a drop in their apparel spending during COVID-19 because they recognized it as "non-essential" due to the lack of need to dress up.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_014
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What was the mindset of consumers towards purchasing clothing during the pandemic?
nodes.answer: Consumers indicated that they thought more about the clothing they already had and focused on purchasing items that filled style holes within their closet.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_015
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did the pandemic impact consumer spending on apparel?
nodes.answer: The pandemic led to changes in consumer spending on apparel, with some individuals spending more on expensive items and others actively seeking discounts for higher quality garments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_016
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What percentage of respondents indicated that they bought apparel for reduced environmental impacts pre-COVID-19?
nodes.answer: On average across seven countries, only 26% of respondents indicated that they bought apparel for reduced environmental impacts before the COVID-19 pandemic.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_017
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: In which countries was the highest level of engagement with the practice of buying ethically-made apparel reported pre-COVID-19?
nodes.answer: The highest levels of engagement with the practice of buying ethically-made apparel pre-COVID-19 were reported in DE (Germany) at 44%, IR (Ireland) at 37%, and US (United States) at 37%.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_018
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did the COVID-19 pandemic impact the buying behaviour of consumers towards ethically-made apparel?
nodes.answer: The pandemic resulted in varied responses from consumers regarding ethically-made apparel purchases. For 54% of respondents, it remained the same, while 32% reported a decrease, and 14% noted an increase in their purchases.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_019
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the social impacts of fast fashion according to NiinimÃƒÆ’Ã‚Æ’Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¤ki (2010)?
nodes.answer: NiinimÃƒÆ’Ã‚Æ’Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¤ki (2010) attributes the social impacts of fast fashion to clothing moving from a utilitarian necessity to fulfilling hedonistic and psychogenic needs.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_020
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why do consumers sometimes dismiss truly sustainable fashion options?
nodes.answer: Consumers may dismiss truly sustainable fashion options due to factors such as price differences, convenience, and perceived value, which can lead them to opt for fast fashion alternatives.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_021
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is it important to increase awareness and knowledge of rental clothing schemes among consumers?
nodes.answer: It is crucial to increase awareness and knowledge of rental clothing schemes among consumers to ensure more sustainable options are known to them, as many participants had not used them but had seen evidence on social media or looked into them a few times.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_022
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why do some people hesitate to pay the true cost of clothing?
nodes.answer: Many individuals may be hesitant to spend what the true cost of clothing should be due to the availability of extremely low-priced items from fast fashion brands like Misguided and Boohoo, which creates unrealistic expectations of clothing prices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_023
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why are consumers often sceptical of rental clothing as a sustainable alternative?
nodes.answer: Consumers are often sceptical of rental clothing as a sustainable alternative due to the novelty of such schemes, which leads to doubts about their sustainability credentials. Additionally, concerns about the fit of clothes, especially for items like dresses that need to fit well, further contribute to consumer scepticism.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_024
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the treatment of workers and the company's selection of suppliers impact workers in the apparel industry?
nodes.answer: The treatment of workers and the choice of suppliers by a company in the apparel industry can greatly impact workers in terms of social, economic, and environmental aspects.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_025
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why does apparel sourcing and manufacturing change quickly in the fast fashion competitive marketplace for U.S. apparel customers?
nodes.answer: Apparel sourcing and manufacturing changes quickly in the fast fashion market based largely on price and time to retail floor, as desired styles change rapidly and competition is fierce.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_026
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the economic sustainability advantages of workers in Sri Lanka producing leggings for U.S. consumption?
nodes.answer: There are significant global economic sustainability advantages to workers producing leggings in Sri Lanka for U.S. consumption, as shown by the wage comparison and cost-effectiveness of production.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_027
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: 3. Why do responsible fashion managers believe they need consumers on board for sustainable choices?
nodes.answer: Responsible fashion managers believe they need consumers on board to develop more sustainable choices in line with customersÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢Ãƒâ€šÃ‚â‚¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚â„¢ perceived value, understanding that collaboration is essential for creating a more sustainable fashion industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_028
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What are some characteristics that lead consumers to fall into the slow fashion segment?
nodes.answer: Consumers in the slow fashion segment acquire apparel made of environmentally preferable fibres and from sources believed to be environmentally preferable, such as second-hand sources, eco-conscious companies, independently owned companies, and home sewing.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_029
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do consumers in the slow fashion segment differ in their awareness of social and environmental responsibility?
nodes.answer: Consumers in the slow fashion segment are hypothesized to be more alert to practices of social and environmental responsibility, as they prioritize sustainable practices when making purchasing decisions for apparel.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_030
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What did Bausch et al. (2021) find regarding the importance of sustainable attributes in online apparel consumers' purchasing decisions?
nodes.answer: Bausch et al. (2021) found that while conventional apparel attributes like fit, comfort, price-performance ratio, and quality are more relevant to consumers, the most important sustainable apparel attributes are the garment's durability, fair wages and working conditions, and environmentally friendly production processes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_031
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the philosophy behind slow fashion according to Nice (2011)?
nodes.answer: According to Nice (2011), the philosophy behind slow fashion is to focus on the individual, reduce fast and high consumption, and promote a balanced approach to social, environmental, and economic aspects.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_032
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do Joy et al. (2015) explain the lack of conflict guilt among young people consuming fast fashion?
nodes.answer: Joy et al. (2015) found that the possibility of having access to clothes very similar to luxury ones has led young people to consume fast fashion without conflict guilt, despite sharing concerns for environmental and social issues.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_033
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How do slow fashion consumers show alignment between their beliefs and their actions?
nodes.answer: Slow fashion consumers demonstrate alignment by agreeing that organizations should have sustainable practices, even though only 38% said they would be loyal to the brand solely for environmental care.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_034
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How can slow fashion stores attract conscious consumers despite the lack of brand loyalty related to sustainability practices?
nodes.answer: Slow fashion stores can invest in using the media to communicate their practices effectively and form a critical mass regarding the need to minimize environmental impact in apparel production.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_035
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What does the Slow Fashion Company prioritize in its brand values?
nodes.answer: The Slow Fashion Company prioritizes environmental issues and aims to make a difference in the environment.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_036
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What is the appeal of fast fashion to consumers?
nodes.answer: Fast fashion appeals to consumers because it offers a larger variety of clothes at lower prices, making it more accessible and appealing in the short term compared to sustainable alternatives.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_037
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: On a 10-point scale, how did respondents rate the importance of second-hand clothes, bio-based clothes, and clothes produced with respect for workers in sustainable fashion?
nodes.answer: Respondents were asked to rate the importance of second-hand clothes, bio-based clothes, and clothes produced with respect for workers on a 10-point scale to evaluate their significance in sustainable fashion.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_038
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Is bio-based clothing produced in an environmentally respectful manner?
nodes.answer: Yes, bio-based clothing is produced in an environmentally respectful manner as it is part of the bioeconomy, which focuses on sustainable and eco-friendly practices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_039
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did the importance of different clothing characteristics affect purchasing decisions according to the survey results?
nodes.answer: The survey results classified clothing characteristics like impact on the environment, brand, price, quality, and trendiness into categories ranging from not important at all to very important in determining clothing purchasing decisions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_040
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the key characteristics that influence respondents' clothing purchasing decisions?
nodes.answer: The key characteristics that influence respondents' clothing purchasing decisions include economic factors, exclusivity, quality-to-price ratio, environmental considerations, and peer influence. Respondents classified these characteristics according to their importance, ranging from not important at all to very important.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_041
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What were the main characteristics prioritized by respondents when purchasing clothes?
nodes.answer: The main characteristics prioritized by respondents when purchasing clothes were making sure the clothes were made with respect for the environment, of good quality, inexpensive, and had a good quality-to-price ratio.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_042
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: What cultural dimension drives sustainable fashion purchasing for Italian consumers, according to the PLS-SEM analysis?
nodes.answer: According to the PLS-SEM analysis, collectivism is the main cultural dimension driving sustainable fashion purchasing for Italian consumers.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_043
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: How do power distance belief, masculinity, and uncertainty avoidance influence Italian consumers' Willingness to Pay for Sustainable Fashion (WTPM)?
nodes.answer: Power distance belief, masculinity, and uncertainty avoidance negatively influence Italian consumers' WTPM for sustainable fashion purchases, according to the analysis.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_044
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: 1. What are some necessary conditions for purchase intention in sustainable fashion, according to recent studies?
nodes.answer: Environmental attitude and concerns are necessary conditions for purchase intention in sustainable fashion, as proven by several studies (Chechnya et al., 2016b; Joplin and RAGAÃ‚Â¶sch, 2021; Kumar et al., 2021).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_045
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the individualism and collectivism orientation continuum impact sustainable fashion consumption?
nodes.answer: The continuum influences sustainable fashion consumption by shaping individuals' values towards social responsibility and in-group priorities, with collectivist-oriented people showing a stronger sense of responsibility towards their social groups.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_046
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does collectivism orientation influence consumers' willingness to pay more for sustainable fashion?
nodes.answer: Consumers with a collectivism orientation, who prioritize values and attitudes rooted in the social system, are more likely to be willing to pay more for sustainable fashion due to the emphasis on preserving face and upholding social responsibility in their decision-making process.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_047
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does a feminine-oriented mindset influence the purchase of sustainable fashion products?
nodes.answer: A feminine-oriented mindset, prioritizing caring for society and people, and not strongly needing products to express status, leads to higher willingness to purchase sustainable fashion products among individuals scoring high on femininity.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_048
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does a masculine-orientated mindset affect willingness to pay for sustainable fashion?
nodes.answer: People with a higher masculine orientation are likely to express lower willingness to pay more for sustainable fashion due to the higher cost compared to conventional fashion.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_049
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does uncertainty avoidance influence willingness to pay more for sustainable fashion?
nodes.answer: Individuals with a high level of uncertainty avoidance are more conservative and prefer clarity and the status quo, leading to potentially lower willingness to pay more for sustainable fashion due to the risks and uncertainties involved in the purchase decision.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_050
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do Italian consumers rate themselves in terms of sustainable fashion consumption?
nodes.answer: Italian consumers rate themselves as conscious and sensitive to sustainable fashion consumption goals, but they express little knowledge and understanding of sustainable practices in the field.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_051
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the negative correlation between masculinity and the Environmental Sustainability Index (ESI) at the country level impact consumers' willingness to pay for sustainable fashion?
nodes.answer: The negative correlation between masculinity and the ESI at the country level, as reported by Park et al. (2007), can impact consumers' willingness to pay for sustainable fashion.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_052
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: How does uncertainty avoidance influence Italian consumersÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢Ãƒâ€šÃ‚â‚¬Ãƒâ€šÃ‚â„¢ willingness to pay more for sustainable fashion?
nodes.answer: Uncertainty avoidance negatively impacts Italian consumers' willingness to pay more for sustainable fashion, as unclear information can deter high uncertainty avoidance individuals from making environmentally conscious purchasing decisions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_053
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why do high uncertainty avoidance consumers in Italy have a lower willingness to pay more for sustainable fashion?
nodes.answer: High uncertainty avoidance consumers in Italy may have a lower willingness to pay more for sustainable fashion due to the lack of clear industry standards in sustainable fashion, leading to confusion and potential greenwashing, which impacts their purchasing decisions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_054
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does labelling for fibre origin and production methods influence consumer behaviour towards sustainable apparel according to Hustled and Bernard?
nodes.answer: Hustled and Bernard found that labelling for fibre origin and production methods can influence consumer willingness to pay for sustainable apparel.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_055
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What factors influence consumers' willingness to pay more for socially responsible fashion products as discussed in the International Journal of Costume Fashion?
nodes.answer: The International Journal of Costume Fashion suggests that factors such as ethical considerations, environmental concerns, and social responsibility contribute to consumers' willingness to pay more for socially responsible fashion products.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_056
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does consumer identity and ideology relate to eco-clothing according to NiinimÃƒÆ’Ã‚Æ’Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¤ki (2010)?
nodes.answer: NiinimÃƒÆ’Ã‚Æ’Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¤ki (2010) explores the relationship between consumer identity and ideology in the context of eco-clothing, highlighting how individuals' values and beliefs influence their choices in sustainable fashion consumption.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_057
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: Why do fashion brands prioritize transparency in their sustainability disclosures?
nodes.answer: Fashion brands prioritize transparency in their sustainability disclosures as they perceive it as their moral responsibility, "perfect" duty, and obligation to showcase responsible corporate citizenship.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_058
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: In what way do the MRCS and MRSSC theories position brands in the fashion industry?
nodes.answer: These theories position brands as moral agents with a perfect duty to be honest and transparent about their sustainability practices, going beyond mere legal compliance or public relations considerations.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_059
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How did brands like H&M symbolize the fashion industry's pre-pandemic ambition regarding transparency?
nodes.answer: Brands like H&M, committed to becoming circular and climate-positive by 2,030 symbolized the industry's pre-pandemic ambition to execute "perfect duties" regarding transparency in their supply chains.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_060
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What is the Fashion Transparency Index, and how does it rank fashion brands?
nodes.answer: The Fashion Transparency Index ranks fashion brands based on the level of information they disclose publicly on their websites and within sustainability reports.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_061
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why do the majority of explored fashion brands consider corporate transparency a non-negotiable obligation?
nodes.answer: The majority of brands understand their non-negotiable obligation to disclose sustainability policies, which is still the most transparent area of sustainability reporting.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_062
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why did YA1 express a change in behaviour regarding checking clothing labels after referencing her clothing diary entry?
nodes.answer: YA1 expressed a change in behaviour regarding checking clothing labels after referencing her clothing diary entry because she realized that some items she thought where wool were actually synthetic, leading her to understand the importance of fabric composition for care instructions and garment longevity.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_063
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What suggestion did Yates and Evans provide regarding eco-labelling on garments and its connection to sustainability?
nodes.answer: Yates and Evans suggested incorporating eco-labelling on garments to increase awareness among householders about the environmental benefits of line-drying. This suggestion aimed to promote sustainable practices in laundry drying for sustainability.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Conscious clothing purchases_qna_064
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How can clothing users become more informed and conscious actors in the sustainability agenda?
nodes.answer: Clothing users can become more informed and conscious actors in the sustainability agenda by understanding the importance of sustainable maximum use, focusing on reducing wash frequency and prolonging clothing wear rather than solely relying on technological advancements.
